answer.text:
On startup Paws runs `recoverOnStartup` (`src/db/recovery.ts`), which first shifts runner leases to account for downtime (up to `offlineBudgetMs`), then loads every work item in the startup states and decides per item what to do (`src/db/recovery.ts:41-55`). The decision comes from `decideStartup` in `src/core/recovery.ts`: an item in the merge queue that isn't mid-run keeps its place, and `mergeCallInFlight` (a `merge_call` row in SQLite) marks whether a merge call may have gone through while Paws was down (`src/core/recovery.ts:95-96`)(`src/db/remote-merges.ts:78-80`). An item whose checkpoint shows a merge was in progress, or a verifying item whose runner still holds its Closeout work, re-verifies instead (`src/core/recovery.ts:97-98`).

Otherwise an item whose runner still holds work resumes in a fresh session with `reattach: true`, resuming from its checkpoint (or its branch if there is none) (`src/core/recovery.ts:99-100`); `recoverOnStartup` recognizes this as reattaching when a `process_restart` resume already exists and skips re-applying the decision so no duplicate job is enqueued (`src/db/recovery.ts:76-86`). A run still active in the lane that was cut short mid-work re-verifies rather than resuming [E4:94,75-82].

Two special paths: an item that already used its one resume and restarted again soon after gets `ask_restart`, which surfaces a Linear question asking whether to start it again (`src/core/recovery.ts:101-102`)(`src/db/recovery.ts:58-61`) — the doc comment says a resume happens "once" and the next start asks (`src/core/recovery.ts:76-79`). Items with a pending capacity wait, pending answer resume, or pending transient retry are left alone so recovery neither spends an attempt nor enqueues a duplicate job (`src/db/recovery.ts:62-64`)(`src/db/recovery.ts:103-113`). Finally, `awaiting_input` items release their run capacity and a single catchup job is enqueued if any such items exist (`src/db/recovery.ts:89-98`). The README corroborates this: "A restart is safe while work is running… Paws reattaches to the same commands after startup, including in-flight Closeout reviews and answer tasks" (`README.md:54`).

This is based on 5 source ranges in 5 files, not the whole repository. Asking again with mode "deep" can follow the remaining leads.
